newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Samsung Display bets on display technology.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Samsung Display bets on display technology.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Display Devices Co, the world's largest maker of colour picture tubes, sees its future in advanced display technology.

"We are developing flat display panels to prepare for a slowdown in demand growth of colour picture and display tubes in the future," said Sun Wook, president and CEO of Samsung Display, a unit of the giant Samsung Group.

The new business of flat display panels will include plasma display panels used in wall-type televisions with ultra-wide screens and thin film transistor liquid crystal displays (TFT LCDs), the most popular display device used in notebook personal computers.
The company believes flat display panels will eventually replace picture and display tubes.
Samsung Display will also broaden its product offerings into light, power-efficient batteries and digitisers, the next generation input device for computers.
Sun said his company hopes to take the lucrative TFT LCD business away from its sister company Samsung Electronics Co Ltd by 1998.
"We have agreed with Samsung Electronics in principle to bring over the TFT LCD business before the year 2000," he said. "But we would like to take it over some time next year."
Samsung Display now only makes colour filters for TFT LCDs.

Analysts said Samsung Electronics was reluctant to give up a potentially profitable business line. However Sun said it was only "desirable" for a company specialising in display products to cover the TFT LCD sector.

Samsung Electronics is expected to see its first profits from the TFT LCD division next year, after investing an estimated 2.1 trillion won ($2.4 billion) to set up production lines over the last three years, they said.
"It's where the growth will be in the future," said Suh Yong-won, electronics analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
"Samsung Electronics would hesitate to give up what could be a very lucrative business after such a heavy investment."
Samsung Display's new passion for advanced display technology does not mean it would abandon the colour picture and display tube business -- its mainstay for the last 27 years.
To counter a global oversupply of low-end products, the company has been shifting to high-end, wider colour display tubes for computor monitors.
Samsung Display's earnings are expected to remain flat in 1997 versus a 164.2 billion won profit last year, while sales would rise to 2.7 trillion in 1997 from 2.46 trillion in 1996.
Sun aims to take 24-25 percent of the global market share of tube sales by 2000 from 16 percent at present.
"Samsung's market share should increase as overseas production expands," said Keon Han, an electronics analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.

Samsung Display now has plants in Malaysia, Germany and Mexico, and is building factories in Shenzhen and Tianjin in China and in Manaus, Brazil. The Commonwealth of Independent States, India and Europe are being considered for plants.

Overseas subsidiaries were expected to generate 25 billion won in net profits this year from 10 billion last year, Sun said. He saw the turnover of overseas subsidiaries rising to 910 billion won this year from 670 billion in 1996.
Sun said he hoped to raise the ratio of tubes produced overseas to 57 percent by 2000 from the current 39 percent.
"Times have changed. We have to be there to deliver goods quickly to meet consumers' fast-changing needs," he said.
